Review only SQL injection in this SQLite lookup. The table name and SQL are constants; handle is the only attacker-controlled string. Authorization is handled separately.
row = db.execute('SELECT public_name FROM directory WHERE handle = ?', (handle,)).fetchone()
better: Secure, 0 SQL-injection issues in this lookup. SQLite binds handle as a value; its punctuation cannot become SQL syntax. Keep the placeholder and separate parameter tuple. Binding handles quotes without hand-written escaping.
worse: Needs changes, 1 SQL-injection issue (CWE-89) in this lookup. SQLite expands handle into SQL before execution, so its punctuation can become syntax. Escape quotes before binding the parameter.
what_is_wrong: The worse answer mistakes bound data for interpolated SQL syntax.

prompt:

what_is_wrong: The worse answer assumes that rejecting multiple statements prevents injection within one statement.

prompt:

Assume a healthy OS random source. Expiration, one-time redemption, transport, storage and account binding are handled correctly elsewhere. A scanner says URL-safe encoding makes these tokens predictable.
